```bash
pnpm run dev
```

### Execute useQuery in a Vue component with <script setup>

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/installation.md

Demonstrates invoking useQuery within a Vue Single-File Component using the <script setup> Composition API syntax.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const { isPending, isFetching, isError, data, error } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: getTodos,
})
</script>

<template>...</template>
```

### useQueryClient(id)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin via Vue injection context. Must be invoked within setup() or an equivalent function that supports injection.

```APIDOC
## function useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient

### Description
Retrieves the `QueryClient` installed by `VueQueryPlugin`, via Vue's `inject`. Must be called inside `setup()` or another function that supports an injection context.

### Parameters
- **id** (`string`, optional, default: `''`) - The `queryClientKey` passed to `VueQueryPlugin` — only needed when multiple `QueryClient`s are installed in the same app.

### Returns
- **QueryClient** - The `QueryClient` instance retrieved from the injection context.

### Throws
- Throws an error if called outside an injection context, or if no `QueryClient` was installed via `VueQueryPlugin`.

### Example
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```
```

### Basic TanStack Solid Query setup with useQuery and QueryClientProvider

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Wrap the application in a QueryClientProvider and pass a QueryClient instance. Inside components, use useQuery with an accessor function returning query options and handle loading, error, and success states using SolidJS control flow components.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Switch, Match, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const query = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={query.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.error}>
          <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isSuccess}>
          <For each={query.data}>{(todo) => <p>{todo.title}</p>}</For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### Fetch data with useQuery in a component

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/vue-query/README.md

Call useQuery in the setup method of a component by passing an object containing queryKey and queryFn.

```tsx
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

export default defineComponent({
  name: 'MyComponent',
  setup() {
    const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })

    return {
      query,
    }
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure custom batch schedulers with setScheduler

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/variables/notifyManager.md

Examples showing how to schedule batches using microtasks, requestAnimationFrame, or custom setTimeout intervals.

```ts
import { notifyManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

// Schedule batches in the next microtask
notifyManager.setScheduler(queueMicrotask)

// Schedule batches before the next frame is rendered
notifyManager.setScheduler(requestAnimationFrame)

// Schedule batches some time in the future
notifyManager.setScheduler((cb) => setTimeout(cb, 10))
```

### Instantiate QueryClient and execute a query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryClient.md

Demonstrates initializing a QueryClient with custom query defaults and performing a query execution.

```ts
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      staleTime: Infinity,
    },
  },
})

await queryClient.query({ queryKey: ['posts'], queryFn: fetchPosts })
```

--------------------------------

### Set up QueryClientProvider and fetch data with createQuery

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/overview.md

Configure QueryClientProvider at the project root and consume createQuery inside child components. Arguments to createQuery must be wrapped in a function to maintain reactivity in Svelte.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: () => fetchTodos(),
  }))
</script>

<div>
  {#if query.isPending}
    <p>Loading...</p>
  {:else if query.isError}
    <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
  {:else if query.isSuccess}
    {#each query.data as todo}
      <p>{todo.title}</p>
    {/each}
  {/if}
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Basic useMutation example in Solid

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/guides/mutations.md

Demonstrates creating a mutation to post data and rendering UI conditionally based on isPending, isError, and isSuccess states.

```tsx
import { Switch, Match, Show } from 'solid-js'

function App() {
  const mutation = useMutation(() => ({
    mutationFn: (newTodo) => {
      return axios.post('/todos', newTodo)
    },
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={mutation.isPending}>Adding todo...</Match>
        <Match when={true}>
          <Show when={mutation.isError}>
            <div>An error occurred: {mutation.error.message}</div>
          </Show>

          <Show when={mutation.isSuccess}>
            <div>Todo added!</div>
          </Show>

          <button
            onClick={() => {
              mutation.mutate({ id: new Date(), title: 'Do Laundry' })
            }}
          >
            Create Todo
          </button>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### createQueryController(host, options, queryClient?)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createQueryController.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to a single query. The returned accessor is callable and provides query state and helper methods including current, refetch, suspense, and destroy. When options is passed as a function, it is re-evaluated during host updates.

```APIDOC
### Function Overview
Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to a single query.

### Signature
```ts
function createQueryController<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryData, TQueryKey>(
  host: ReactiveControllerHost,
  options: Accessor<CreateQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryData, TQueryKey>>,
  queryClient?: QueryClient
): QueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>;
```

### Type Parameters
- **TQueryFnData** (default: `unknown`)
- **TError** (default: `Error`)
- **TData** (default: `TQueryFnData`)
- **TQueryData** (default: `TQueryFnData`)
- **TQueryKey** (extends `readonly unknown[]`, default: `readonly unknown[]`)

### Parameters
- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the query subscription.
- **options** (`Accessor<CreateQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryData, TQueryKey>>`) - Query observer options, or a getter function that returns options. When a function is provided, it is re-read during host updates.
- **queryClient** (`QueryClient`, optional) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns
- **QueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>** - An accessor for the latest query result with query helper methods (`current`, `refetch`, `suspense`, `destroy`).

### Usage Example
```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createQueryController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class TodosView extends LitElement {
  private readonly todos = createQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: async () => fetch('/api/todos').then((r) => r.json()),
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.todos()

    if (query.isPending) return html`Loading...`
    if (query.isError) return html`Error`

    return html`<ul>${query.data.map((todo) => html`<li>${todo.title}</li>`)}</ul>`
  }
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Instantiate and subscribe to InfiniteQueryObserver

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/InfiniteQueryObserver.md

Demonstrates creating an InfiniteQueryObserver with pagination options and subscribing to query state changes.

```ts
const observer = new InfiniteQueryObserver(queryClient, {
  queryKey: ['projects'],
  queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
  initialPageParam: 0,
  getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextCursor,
})

const unsubscribe = observer.subscribe((result) => console.log(result))
```

### createInfiniteQueryController(host, options, queryClient?)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createInfiniteQueryController.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query. The returned accessor provides the latest query result and exposes helper methods like fetchNextPage and fetchPreviousPage. If queryClient is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest QueryClientProvider context.

```APIDOC
## createInfiniteQueryController

### Description
Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query. The returned accessor is callable and also exposes `current`, `refetch`, `fetchNextPage`, `fetchPreviousPage`, and `destroy`. When `options` is a function, it is re-read during host updates so query keys and options can follow reactive host state. If `queryClient` is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest connected `QueryClientProvider`.

### Signature
```ts
function createInfiniteQueryController<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>(
   host: ReactiveControllerHost,
   options: Accessor<CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>>,
   queryClient?: QueryClient
): InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>;
```

### Type Parameters
- **TQueryFnData** - Defaults to `unknown`. Type of data returned by the query function.
- **TError** - Defaults to `Error`. Error type for the query.
- **TData** - Defaults to `InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>`. Type of accumulated infinite query data.
- **TQueryKey** - Defaults to `readonly unknown[]`. Type of the query key.
- **TPageParam** - Defaults to `unknown`. Type of the page parameter.

### Parameters
- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the infinite query subscription.
- **options** (`Accessor<CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>>`) - Infinite query observer options, or a getter function that returns options.
- **queryClient** (`QueryClient`, optional) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns
- **InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>** - An accessor for the latest infinite query result with page helper methods.

### Example
```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createInfiniteQueryController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class ProjectsView extends LitElement {
  private readonly projects = createInfiniteQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextCursor,
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.projects()

    return html`
      <button ?disabled=${!query.hasNextPage} @click=${() => this.projects.fetchNextPage()}>
        Load more
      </button>
    `
  }
}
```
```

### useQuery<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>(options, queryClient?)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Executes a query in Solid applications and returns a reactive query result as a Solid store. It tracks fetch states and handles caching.

```APIDOC
### Call Signature

```ts
function useQuery<TQueryFnData = unknown, TError = Error, TData = TQueryFnData, TQueryKey extends readonly unknown[] = readonly unknown[]>(
  options: UndefinedInitialDataOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>,
  queryClient?: () => QueryClient
): UseQueryResult<TData, TError>;
```

### Type Parameters

- **TQueryFnData** = `unknown`
- **TError** = `Error`
- **TData** = `TQueryFnData`
- **TQueryKey** *extends* `readonly unknown[]` = `readonly unknown[]`

### Parameters

- **options** (`UndefinedInitialDataOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>`) - An accessor returning the query options to use.
- **queryClient** (`() => QueryClient`, optional) - An accessor for a custom `QueryClient`. If not provided, the one from the nearest context is used.

### Returns

- **UseQueryResult<TData, TError>** - The current query result as a Solid store. `status` is `pending` if there is no cached data to display, `error` if the last fetch attempt failed, or `success` if the query has data to display. Contains `isPending`, `isSuccess`, and `isError` derived booleans for convenience.
```

### Configure TestBed with a fresh QueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/testing.md

Sets up TestBed with an isolated QueryClient instance configured with retry disabled for faster test failures. Use provideTanStackQuery or provideQueryClient to provide it in test modules without including withDevtools.

```ts
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retry: false, // ✅ faster failure tests
    },
  },
})

TestBed.configureTestingModule({
  providers: [provideTanStackQuery(queryClient)],
})
```

### Fetch data using useQuery with initialData

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Demonstrates setting `initialData` in `useQuery` so `data` is defined immediately without needing a pending check. Even if refetching fails, existing data remains accessible alongside the error state.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'

function Posts() {
  // `data` is `Post[]`, never `undefined`, thanks to `initialData` — even if a refetch fails,
  // so the list stays visible alongside the error.
  const { data, isError, error } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
    initialData: [],
  })

  return (
    <div>
      {isError ? <span>Error: {error.message}</span> : null}
      <ul>
        {data.map((post) => <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>)}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Using useQuery with initialData in Solid

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Demonstrates configuring useQuery with initialData in a Solid component so data is never undefined and stays visible if refetching fails.

```tsx
import { For } from 'solid-js'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/solid-query'

function Posts() {
  // `postsQuery.data` is never `undefined`, thanks to `initialData` — even if a refetch fails, so the
  // list stays visible alongside the error.
  const postsQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
    initialData: [],
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      {postsQuery.isError ? <span>Error: {postsQuery.error.message}</span> : null}
      <ul>
        <For each={postsQuery.data}>{(post) => <li>{post.title}</li>}</For>
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Infer query type with HttpClient get

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/typescript.md

Passes a type parameter to Angular HttpClient's get method so injectQuery infers the resulting data array.

```angular-ts
@Component({
  template: `@let data = query.data();`,
  //               ^? data: Group[] | undefined
})
class MyComponent {
  http = inject(HttpClient)

  query = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['groups'],
    queryFn: () => lastValueFrom(this.http.get<Group[]>('/groups')),
  }))
}
```

### setEventListener(setup)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/FocusManager.md

Sets a custom event listener used to determine the focus state. The setup function receives a callback to manually set or re-evaluate focus.

```APIDOC
## setEventListener(setup)

### Description
`setEventListener` can be used to set a custom event listener that will be used to determine the focus state. The provided `setup` function receives a `setFocused` callback: call it with a `boolean` to manually set the focus state, or with no arguments to re-evaluate the current focus state and notify subscribers.

### Signature
```ts
setEventListener(setup: SetupFn): void;
```

### Parameters
- **setup** (`SetupFn`) - Required - A function setting up the event listeners and returning an unsubscribe/cleanup function.

### Returns
`void`

### Example
```ts
import { focusManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const listener = () => handleFocus()
  // Listen to visibilitychange
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.addEventListener) {
    window.addEventListener('visibilitychange', listener, false)
  }

  return () => {
    // Be sure to unsubscribe if a new handler is set
    window.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', listener)
  }
})
```
```
